claim: A published human PSC-derived assembloid combined microglia with oligodendrocyte-containing neural organoids and measured cross-cell consequences with single-cell profiles, oligodendrocyte-lineage abundance, MBP staining, lipid assays, and electron microscopy, providing a technical precedent for testing whether a microglial perturbation changes myelination-related function.
future_grounding_route: Treat as a platform precedent only. A project route must use MS-relevant, direction-resolved perturbations, crossed independent donors, blinded functional readouts, and a prespecified transfer test rather than importing the source's TREX1 mechanism.

project_finding_reference.finding_id: proposed direction-resolving human microglia perturbation program

project_use: External method context for adding oligodendrocyte and myelin consequences to a future microglial perturbation screen; not evidence for TREX1, statins, or an MS target.
relationship_note: This supplies a cross-cell functional assay missing from a transcript-only screen, but it models a different genetic disease mechanism and does not validate transfer to MS progression.

source.citation: Goldberg et al. TREX1 is required for microglial cholesterol homeostasis and oligodendrocyte terminal differentiation in human neural assembloids. Molecular Psychiatry. 2024.
source.label: Human microglia-oligodendrocyte assembloid

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: CC BY article; metadata and short paraphrase retained
source_terms.reuse_notes: This repository stores only bibliographic metadata and a short method paraphrase.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced this assembloid experiment or independently grounded its source-reported biological mechanism.
